question.problem:
| $x$ | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $7$ | $5$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

Consider the data sets above. You are given that $\overset{―}{x}=2$ and $\overset{―}{y}=3.$ Find the equation of the corresponding linear regression line. Round the slope and the $y$-intercept to $1$ decimal place if necessary.
question.worked_solution:
The equation of the regression line is given by

$$
y=mx+b,
$$

where 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{S}_{xy}}{{S}_{xx}},\,b=\overset{―}{y}-m\overset{―}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute $m:$

- First, we compute the sum in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =(0-2)(7-3)+(1-2)(5-3) \\  & +(3-2)(1-3)+(4-2)(-1-3) \\  & =(-2)(4)+(-1)(2)+(1)(-2)+(2)(-4) \\  & =-8-2-2-8 \\  & =-20\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, we compute the sum in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =(0-2)^{2}+(1-2)^{2}+(3-2)^{2}+(4-2)^{2} \\  & =4+1+1+4 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting into the formula for $m,$ we obtain 

$$
m=\frac{-20}{10}=-2.
$$

Next, we substitute into the formula for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =\overset{―}{y}-m\overset{―}{x} \\  & =3-(-2)\cdot 2 \\  & =3+4 \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the regression line is

$$
y=-2x+7.
$$
